# `minority-naming-style`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: none · Default: off · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a function, type, or constant whose casing differs from the project's
dominant casing for that declaration kind.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

A project that deliberately differs from the official guide still benefits from
being internally predictable.

## When it fires

A convention requires at least 20 declarations and a 90% majority. Foreign and
generated declarations are excluded. A struct without fields is a namespace,
which Zig style names like a value, so it is not a type name; a type spelled
like `IORING_OP` mirrors a C or ABI name and is left out too.

With [`non-idiomatic-name`](non-idiomatic-name.md) enabled, a name that breaks
Zig's convention for its kind is left to that rule, which reports it with the
project's convention when the two differ and works in the editor. This rule
then adds the names that follow Zig's guide but not the casing the project
chose, such as a camelCase function in a snake_case project.
